title: prefill conductor: stable prefetch orchestration + quant-tier telemetry pilot
author: Maya Hernandez
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces a lightweight 'prefill-conductor' to stabilize and automate tenant prefetch/prefill behavior as part of our cost-optimization automation workstream. The conductor combines: (1) deterministic default prefetch policies for common workload shapes, (2) a quant-tier hinting layer to prefer lower-precision model variants safely, and (3) telemetry hooks to measure unit economics (tokens-per-inference, effective cost per 1k tokens, cache-hit delta) across deployments.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token unit cost for mid-sized tenants by enabling safe, automated prefill defaults and quantization suggestions.
- Make prefill decisions observable and rollable: metrics + rollout controls + safe fallbacks.
- Provide a small, pluggable orchestrator that can be toggled per-tenant and integrated with existing policy DSLs.

What changed (summary):
- services/prefill/conductor: new orchestrator that schedules prefill tasks, credits prefetch budgets, and computes quant-tier hints from sampled telemetry.
- config/prefill/defaults.yaml: a compact rule set of deterministic defaults (shapes: short-chat, long-prompt, embedding-burst) and safe thresholds.
- internal/quant/registry: added quant-tier metadata and compatibility checks (float16, q4_0, q4_1) used by the conductor when proposing fallbacks.
- observability/metrics/prefill_metrics.go: cost-focused metrics (prefill_tokens_total, prefill_cache_hit_ratio, prefetched_token_cost_estimate_usd).
- cli/econ: added 'econ dry-run prefill' that simulates prefill decisions for a tenant given historical traces and prints expected cost delta.
- docs/operation/prefill-runbook.md: runbook for enabling the conductor, rollback steps, and SLI/SLO adjustments.
- tests/e2e/prefill_integration_test.go: synthetic workloads validating safety boundaries and no-regression for 95th-pct latency.

Commits (high-level):
1) add prefill conductor scaffold + initial scheduling loop
2) add quant-tier hinting and compatibility matrix
3) wire telemetry metrics + prom labels for tenant_id, profile
4) add CLI dry-run and export format for cost simulation
5) docs and runbook, tests and small fixes after reviewer feedback

Changed areas/files (key paths):
- services/prefill/conductor/manager.go
- services/prefill/conductor/scheduler.go
- config/prefill/defaults.yaml
- internal/quant/registry.go
- observability/metrics/prefill_metrics.go
- cli/econ/commands.go
- docs/operation/prefill-runbook.md
- tests/e2e/prefill_integration_test.go
- pkg/telemetry/labels.go
- scripts/ci/prefill-smoketest.yaml

Design notes and safe defaults:
- The conductor never forces quantization: it emits a hint and a cost vs quality delta estimate. Routing decisions still require an explicit per-tenant opt-in for quant tier fallback (we default to suggestion-only for existing tenants).
- Prefill budgets are soft by default: conductor awards a small token budget per tenant per minute and drops the prefetch if latency SLOs are at risk.
- Compatibility checks ensure we do not suggest a quant tier that lacks kernel support for the target hardware (fallback to float16).

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests for schedule budgeting and quant compatibility checks (coverage: services/prefill/* ~ 78%).
- Integration e2e under synthetic short-chat and embedding-burst workloads; validated no latency regression >2% for P95 and improved median token cost by ~9% in the embedding-burst scenario.
- CI smoke: flakey e2e fix added after first run (see checks).
- Dry-run CLI validated on 3 tenant traces; exported CSVs used to seed the onboarding demo.

Rollout plan:
- Stage: auto-deploy to staging after merge, run 24h telemetry; compare prefetched_token_cost_estimate_usd vs baseline.
- Canary: enable suggestion-only mode for 10% of tenants, collect quality metrics for two weeks.
- Opt-in: tenant admins can flip to 'fallback enabled' via console/CLI for aggressive cost savings.
- Full rollout: gated on quality regression <= 1% on tracked prompt-sets, and cost reduction >= 4% for target cohorts.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: over-aggressive quant hints could reduce answer quality. Mitigation: suggestions only; quant fallback requires tenant opt-in and quality canaries.
- Risk: prefill could increase peak GPU utilization. Mitigation: budgeted prefill token caps + cluster-level admission control.

Related work and notes:
- Follow-up planned: integration with the 'prefill-heatmap' exporter and a multi-tenant simulator in the econ-sandbox. See linked Linear ENG-8901.

If you want to test locally: bin/rdwctl prefill simulate --tenant <id> --trace sample-trace.json

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] e2e smoke test added
- [x] Docs/runbook added
- [x] Telemetry metrics instrumented
- [x] CLI dry-run implemented

review_thread: Ethan Cole (reviewer): Can we make the default suggestion window configurable by tenant? Some customers with bursty embeddings might want shorter windows.
Maya Hernandez (author): Added tenant-level override in defaults.yaml and documented the CLI flag. Default remains 60s to stay conservative.
Priya Nair (reviewer): e2e flaked on first run; I see we reran CI. Please add an explicit wait-for-kernel-availability check before suggesting q4 tiers.
Maya Hernandez (author): Added compatibility probe and a unit test for kernels not present on older nodes. Also added cluster-level admission control comments in the runbook.
Lukas Vogel (reviewer): The telemetry labels look good, but can we include model_variant and sequence_bucket for better sliceability?
Maya Hernandez (author): Included model_variant and seq_bucket labels (lightweight). Confirmed metric cardinality stayed within acceptable bounds during staging.
Ethan Cole (approver): LGTM after fixes. Approving for merge.
merge_outcome: merged via squash; auto-deploy to staging triggered; feature gate defaulted to suggestion-only
release_notes: Introduces a prefill conductor that automates safe prefetch defaults and emits quant-tier hints. Adds econ dry-run CLI to simulate cost impact and new telemetry metrics to monitor prefilling economics. Safe-by-default: suggestions only unless tenant opts-in to quant fallbacks.
notes_for_oncall: If prefill_metrics.prefilled_token_cost_estimate_usd increases unexpectedly, flip 'prefill.enabled' to false for affected tenants and check conductor logs at services/prefill/ for budget saturation warnings.
